title: WhatsApp user guide
screenshot_notice: Screenshots show local development screens. Available fields, values, sender accounts and actions depend on your site configuration and permissions.

guides.title: Find your way around
guides.summary: Navigate hospital messaging, appointment reminders and follow-ups.

screenshots.caption: Messaging workspace: inbox shortcuts, summary cards and User guide.

steps.title: Sign in with your usual account
steps.detail: Use your existing Frappe login. A System Manager assigns Whatsapp Editor or Whatsapp Admin; a separate WhatsApp login is not needed.

steps.title: Open WhatsApp Messaging
steps.detail: Select WhatsApp Messaging in Desk’s app chooser. Riverbend Hospital’s reception team uses Messaging for patient conversations and appointment updates.

steps.title: Expand a sidebar group
steps.detail: Overview opens the messaging workspace. Expand Messaging for Inbox, Conversations, Messages, Media and Recipients. Templates contains reusable content and shared fields; Automation contains campaigns, flows, schedules and its overview. Document delivery groups rules and deliveries. Delivery & logs contains sending history and diagnostics; Administration contains its overview, Senders and Integration settings. User guide stays at the bottom. Your permissions determine which links are visible.

steps.title: Use the cards and guide
steps.detail: Cards open the matching list or inbox filter. Open User guide from any workspace or the app sidebar; search by a task or a button name.

guides.check: You can open the workspaces allowed by your role. A fresh installation can correctly show zero records.
guides.note: If the app is missing, refresh Desk and ask your System Manager to check installation and your existing roles. A disabled outbound banner means browsing is available but sends are blocked.
guides.description: This explains how the app is organized so you can find the tools you need. Messaging contains conversations and message history, Templates & Automation contains message rules and scheduled work, and Administration contains connection settings and troubleshooting tools.

guides.title: Find or start a conversation
guides.summary: Find a patient conversation or start a thread from Patient Services.

screenshots.caption: New conversation asks for a sender and an international recipient number.

steps.title: Open Inbox
steps.detail: From Messaging, choose Inbox. Select Riverbend Patient Services or All business numbers, search for Meera Rao or another patient, and use the status and assignment filters.

steps.title: Use your unread view
steps.detail: Choose Unread to see incoming messages you have not read. Reading a visible thread updates your own unread count, not another agent’s count.

steps.title: Start a thread if needed
steps.detail: Choose New conversation, select Riverbend Patient Services and enter the patient’s international number with its country code. Choose Open conversation.

steps.title: Review before composing
steps.detail: Confirm the sender and recipient in the thread. A new conversation does not send a message or establish a reply window.

guides.check: The selected thread opens. Older messages and additional conversations can be loaded with their respective Load more controls.
guides.note: No senders available means a System Manager must configure an account first. Local read state does not send a WhatsApp read receipt.
guides.description: This groups messages between one recipient and one sender account into a conversation. You can search existing conversations, filter them by status, assignment or unread messages, and open a new conversation using a recipient’s phone number. Opening a conversation creates a place to exchange messages; it does not send anything by itself.

guides.title: Reply to a message
guides.summary: Reply to a patient and follow the message’s delivery status.

screenshots.caption: Message box with send arrow, Template, Emoji, Attach and a character counter.
Desktop inbox with conversation list, timeline and recipient details.

steps.title: Open the right thread
steps.detail: Confirm the sender, recipient and You can reply now notice. For a reply to a specific incoming message, choose that message’s Reply action.

steps.title: Write your reply
steps.detail: Write in the message box. Add an emoji with Emoji, or attach an image or PDF with Attach. The counter shows 4,096 characters for text or 1,024 for an attachment caption. Your draft stays while switching conversations within this page session.

steps.title: Send the reply
steps.detail: Choose the send arrow at the top right of the message box once, or press Ctrl+Enter (Command+Enter on Mac). The message first shows Waiting to send; check Delivered or Read for its later progress.

steps.title: Check the timeline
steps.detail: Look for the new message and its status. If the reply window has closed, choose Template in the bottom toolbar.

guides.check: The message appears in the timeline with a status. Delivered or Read requires a corresponding provider receipt.
guides.note: Send reply is unavailable when sending is off, the contact has been blocked or more than 24 hours have passed since their last message. The explanation above the reply box tells you what to do. Your draft stays when switching conversations in this tab, but reloading or leaving the page clears it.
guides.description: This lets you write a text response in an existing conversation. The app saves the message, adds it to the sending queue and shows its progress in the conversation. Normal replies are available while the reply window is open and sending is allowed.

guides.title: Send an image or PDF
guides.summary: Share visit instructions as a private PDF or image.

screenshots.caption: Private file uploader opened from Attach image or PDF.

steps.title: Check the reply window
steps.detail: Open the conversation and confirm You can reply now. Attachments use the normal reply path.

steps.title: Choose a supported file
steps.detail: Choose Attach image or PDF and upload the visit-instructions PDF (up to 20 MB), or one JPEG or PNG (up to 5 MB). The app checks the actual file type as well as size.

steps.title: Review the attachment
steps.detail: The selected filename appears in the composer. Add an optional caption. Choose Remove attachment if the wrong file was selected.

steps.title: Queue and inspect
steps.detail: Choose Send reply. Open a received attachment from the timeline only when its download is ready.

guides.check: The attachment is linked to the queued message and stored privately. Incoming unsupported files show a placeholder or blocked state.
guides.note: Uploading a file alone does not send it. If a file is rejected, use one of the supported types; renaming a file extension does not change its actual type. WhatsApp Media uploads default to Private. Selecting an existing public library file is rejected; upload a private copy instead.
guides.description: This lets you include a JPEG image, PNG image or PDF in a reply. The app checks the file’s type and size, stores it privately and includes it when you queue the message. The attachment stays connected to the message so permitted users can refer to it later.

guides.title: Use an approved WhatsApp template
guides.summary: Confirm an appointment outside the reply window with an approved template.

screenshots.caption: Approved template parameter dialog: review the body and fill each numbered parameter.

steps.title: Check messaging permissions
steps.detail: An administrator must record the contact’s permission before you send a template. Blocked contacts cannot receive messages.

steps.title: Choose Send a template
steps.detail: Choose Send a template, select appointment_confirmation and its language for Patient Services, then choose Review message. Only supported WhatsApp-approved templates for this business number are listed.

steps.title: Fill in the message details
steps.detail: Review the wording and fill each Message detail field. Each replaces a numbered placeholder, such as {{1}}. In the hospital walkthrough, Message detail 1 is Meera Rao and Message detail 2 is OPD-1042. Check the name and appointment reference before sending.

steps.title: Send the template
steps.detail: Choose Send template, then check the thread status. If the catalogue is empty, ask an Admin to sync approved templates from the sender form. Templates also provides the Meta review status and rejection guidance for authored content.

guides.check: The request uses the selected approved template and language with your supplied parameters.
guides.note: Inbox sending uses supported approved templates with a text body and optional fixed text header and footer from the sender’s Meta account. To author or correct the wording, open Templates, choose Meta-approved template mode and manage its review there. Campaigns reference the reusable template for automated or bulk sending.
guides.description: This lets you send a message using wording already approved by WhatsApp, including when the normal reply window is closed. You select the template and language, fill in its required values and queue the message. The app checks that the template belongs to the sender’s account and that the recipient is eligible to receive it.

guides.title: Assign conversations and track progress
guides.summary: Coordinate patient conversations between reception staff.

screenshots.caption: Assign conversation dialog: a supervisor can choose a team member or Not assigned.

steps.title: Assign a conversation to yourself
steps.detail: Open a conversation and choose Assign to me. Choose Remove assignment when you no longer need to handle it.

steps.title: Update your conversation’s status
steps.detail: Use the Status selector: Open for work that needs attention, Waiting when awaiting a response, and Resolved when finished. Editors must be assigned to the conversation to change its status.

steps.title: Reassign when supervising
steps.detail: Admin and System Manager can choose Assign to someone, select a Team member or Not assigned, and choose Save assignment.

steps.title: Review activity
steps.detail: Conversation history records assignment and status changes. A new incoming message reopens a resolved conversation.

guides.check: The assigned team member and status update, with an entry in Conversation history. Use Assigned to me or Unassigned to find conversations.
guides.note: Assignment coordinates work; app users still share permitted history and sending access. If another agent changed the thread first, refresh before trying again.
guides.description: This records who will handle a conversation and whether it needs attention, is waiting for a response or is finished. Choose Assign to me to take responsibility, or Remove assignment to release your own conversation. Supervisors can assign conversations to another team member.

guides.title: Link a business record
guides.summary: Connect a patient conversation to the relevant appointment or follow-up record.

screenshots.caption: Link a record dialog with Record type and Record fields.

steps.title: Open conversation details
steps.detail: On desktop use the right-hand details panel. On a phone open the thread and choose Details.

steps.title: Choose Link a record
steps.detail: Choose Link a record, select the Record type and Choose a record, then choose Link record. The walkthrough links Meera Rao’s OPD-1042 follow-up task.

steps.title: Open the linked record
steps.detail: Use its button under Linked records to return to the business document.

steps.title: Review activity
steps.detail: Check Conversation history to see who linked a record and when.

guides.check: The explicit link appears in the conversation. Sending from a readable source record also creates an explicit link.
guides.note: Linking does not grant access to the business record. A matching phone number alone does not link records.
guides.description: This connects a conversation to a specific business record so users can move between the messages and the record they concern. The app checks that the user can read the record before creating the link. The link is saved with the conversation and recorded in its activity history.

guides.title: Send from a business record
guides.summary: Send an appointment reminder from the related business record.

screenshots.caption: A fictional ToDo record with its configured WhatsApp message action.

steps.title: Check the campaign
steps.detail: Configure an enabled campaign for the business DocType, reusable Message Template, sender and recipient field. Select None or Custom for a manual action. Bulk campaigns use preview and start instead.

steps.title: Open the business record
steps.detail: Open a readable appointment or follow-up record. In this walkthrough, the appointment follow-up is a ToDo task. Open WhatsApp Messaging and choose Send appointment reminder, the Button Label configured on the campaign.

steps.title: Run the configured action
steps.detail: Select the intended template action and review any prompt shown. The app creates a durable request rather than sending directly from the browser.

steps.title: Open View Conversation
steps.detail: Use View Conversation when an explicit conversation link exists. Check the timeline and delivery state there.

guides.check: A single source-scoped request is queued and the conversation is explicitly linked to its readable source record.
guides.note: If the action is missing, ask an Admin to check the campaign’s DocType, event, recipient mapping and disabled flag. Source permission and sender eligibility are checked again before dispatch.
guides.description: This sends a message from a business record using a configured campaign. The app reads the recipient and approved message details from that record, creates a sending request and links the conversation back to the source. This reduces repeated typing and makes it clear which record the message concerns.

guides.title: Record consent or stop sending
guides.summary: Record appointment-message consent or stop sending to a patient.

screenshots.caption: Messaging permissions dialog shown to Admin and System Manager.

steps.title: Open the recipient’s thread
steps.detail: Confirm the contact’s WhatsApp number in Details before changing messaging permissions.

steps.title: Choose Messaging permissions
steps.detail: Choose Messaging permissions. Select This contact has agreed to receive messages only when they have given permission. Under How was permission received?, enter its source, such as Appointment booking form.

steps.title: Block messages when needed
steps.detail: Enable Block messages to this number to stop all outgoing messages to this contact. Choose Save permissions.

steps.title: Review the result
steps.detail: Details shows the updated permissions, and Conversation history records the change. The app checks the permissions again before sending a waiting message.

guides.check: The contact’s permission or blocked state is saved. Blocking stops both replies and template messages.
guides.note: Editors can view messaging permissions but cannot change them. Never record permission unless the contact has actually agreed to receive messages.
guides.description: This records whether a contact has agreed to receive messages and how that permission was received. An administrator can block outgoing messages to a number, including replies and templates. These permissions are checked again before sending.

guides.title: Manage reusable media files
guides.summary: Keep visit-instruction images and PDFs ready for templates.
guides.description: This saves a private image or PDF for reuse in message templates and uploads it to WhatsApp Cloud for the selected Sender. The app checks the file, fills in its format and size, and shows the cloud upload status and Media ID. Saving media does not send a message to anyone.

screenshots.caption: Quick Entry asks for Label, Sender and File, then shows the detected type, size and private preview.
The saved form shows file details and the separate WhatsApp Cloud upload result.

steps.title: Add a reusable file
steps.detail: Open WhatsApp Messaging → Media and choose Add WhatsApp Media. Enter a recognizable Label, such as Riverbend visit instructions, or leave it blank to use the filename. Choose the Sender account, then a private JPEG/PNG image up to 5 MB, or PDF up to 20 MB.

steps.title: Check and save
steps.detail: Review the private preview and detected size, then choose Save. The app fills in the file details and queues a background cloud upload after saving. Both Enable Outbound Requests in WhatsApp Settings and the selected Sender must be enabled. Uploading a file alone does not save the media entry, and saving media does not send a message.

steps.title: Check the cloud result
steps.detail: Open the saved record. Pending or Uploading means the upload is waiting or running. Uploaded shows the WhatsApp Media ID and upload time. Blocked explains a setting or access problem; Failed explains an upload problem. Correct it and choose Upload / Retry. IDs are refreshed when needed; Refresh cloud upload lets you request a fresh ID.

steps.title: Use the file in a template
steps.detail: Choose the saved Ready media under Content in a Message Template. Its Message Text becomes Caption. A message using the same Sender and file can reuse its current cloud Media ID. Another Sender, an expired ID or a file without a completed cloud upload uses a separate upload when that message is sent.

steps.title: Replace or remove a selection
steps.detail: Open the media entry in the full form. Remove selection clears the choice without deleting the stored file. Choose a replacement and explicitly Save to apply it. File details update, the previous cloud ID is cleared, and a new upload is queued when enabled. Saving an existing entry with no file marks it Needs File and prevents its use in templates.

steps.title: Review older records
steps.detail: Existing media is not uploaded automatically during the update. Choose its Sender and Save or Upload / Retry. Needs Attention means an old file could not be verified; choose a supported private replacement. Legacy URL records retain the URL for reference and require a private upload before use. The app does not fetch that URL or turn public files private.

guides.check: The saved file is Ready, shows the correct type and size, and appears in the template picker. With the Sender and Outbound Requests enabled and the media worker running, its Cloud Upload Status becomes Uploaded and a WhatsApp Media ID appears.
guides.note: Notes are internal library notes, not outgoing captions. Removing a selection or deleting the library entry preserves stored files and existing message attachments; it does not delete an upload from Meta. File deletion is a separate action in File Manager. Changes affect future message preparation; queued messages retain their prepared file snapshots.

guides.title: Build a conversation flow
guides.summary: Guide people through menus, collect a request and hand over to reception.
guides.audience: Admin · System Manager; Editors can preview and handle conversations
guides.description: A conversation flow replies when someone messages your business number. It can show menus, collect answers, send a saved template and pass the conversation to staff. A template step can find an existing record using the contact’s phone number and your filters. The hospital starter collects appointment requests for reception to confirm; it does not book appointments.

steps.title: Create a draft
steps.detail: Open WhatsApp Templates & Automation → Conversation Flows. Choose Create hospital starter flow, select your business WhatsApp number and choose Create draft. You can also create a flow from New.

steps.title: Edit messages and choices
steps.detail: The Workflow map shows connected cards and a dot for each branch. Drag a dot onto another card to connect it, or click a branch to choose an existing step or add a connected step. Drag cards to arrange; Save keeps their positions. Use Undo/Redo to reverse edits. Choose a card’s pencil to edit its message or menu choices, then Apply step and Save. Menu labels must be unique and at most 24 characters. Fit map, Expand map, Auto arrange and Step list help you explore. Fill in hospital information before publishing.

steps.title: Reuse a template and find its record
steps.detail: Add or edit a step, choose Template and select a saved text template. Flow values lets you choose an earlier answer, contact name, contact phone number or fixed text for each variable. Record lookup finds records of the template’s Source DocType using the contact’s WhatsApp number and your filters. For appointment confirmation, first show the current number and ask whether it is registered with the hospital. Yes continues; No asks for the registered number using a Phone question. An entered number matching the WhatsApp contact continues; a different number is not looked up. The bot asks the person to message from their registered WhatsApp number or contact reception for registration help. Appointment details are only shown for the current WhatsApp number. In the template step, select Patient → Mobile, Status equals Scheduled, and Most recently created. This uses booking creation time, not appointment date or last edit; no date question is needed. Choose reception for no booking or ambiguous registered contacts. Other flows can keep Require a single matching record. Phone numbers must include the country code.

steps.title: Try the conversation
steps.detail: Choose Try flow. Select menu options or type in Preview reply. Test the booking, information and reception paths. For record lookup, choose one fictional matching record, no matching record or multiple matching records. The preview uses fictional values, does not query patient records and sends no WhatsApp messages.

steps.title: Publish when ready
steps.detail: Choose Publish and enable to run the saved draft. Only one flow can be active for a business number. Enable Inbound, Outbound and Automation in WhatsApp Settings, and keep the background worker running. Changes saved afterward remain a draft until you publish again.

steps.title: Handle a reception request
steps.detail: In the Inbox, open Details → Flow details to read the collected department, name and preferred date. Assign to me or send a manual reply to pause automatic replies. Confirm appointment availability yourself. Allow menu requests releases the conversation and waits for the contact to type menu; it does not send a message immediately.

guides.check: A new message starts the published menu when its start rule matches. Menu selections route to the correct step, saved answers are visible in Flow details, and handoff stops automatic replies. Old menu selections and repeated webhook events do not create another reply.
guides.note: Meta templates must be approved before publishing a linked flow; local messages need an open reply window. Media templates are not supported in flow steps yet. Shared field approvals and the publishing user’s record permissions apply. If a template, record or approval changes before sending, the reply is held for review. The flow does not book appointments. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD and must be today or later; three unrecognised answers hand over to reception.

screenshots.caption: Workflow map with connected hospital menu steps, branch labels and canvas controls.
Training preview with the hospital menu and appointment-request answers.
Template step with contact matching, appointment filters and reception fallback branches.
Choosing No asks for the registered hospital number before looking up an appointment.
A different entered number shows registration help; its appointments are not looked up.

guides.title: Create and review a message template
guides.summary: Write reusable message content and manage its Meta review in one template.

screenshots.caption: Reusable content: sender, source fields, message editor and Live Preview.
Message Text and inserted fields appear beside the live message preview.
Hospital welcome draft with separate Header, Message Text and Footer fields beside the live preview.
Review screen with rejection reason, Meta recommendation and a suggested fix.
A System Manager approves shared message fields once for all templates using that source DocType.
Insert field includes readable Single DocTypes under Static sources.
Local media changes Message Text to Caption and shows the attachment in Live Preview.

steps.title: Create reusable content
steps.detail: Open Templates & Automation → Templates. Add Appointment confirmation, choose Riverbend Patient Services in Sender, and select the source DocType used for personalization. Select Local message for free-form content or Meta-approved template for wording that must be reviewed by Meta.

steps.title: Import existing Meta content when needed
steps.detail: Open the Sender and choose Sync approved templates. Review the list, choose a Source DocType and import selected entries. Imports preserve Header, Message Text and Footer. Map every numbered variable using Variables & Review Examples before using the content in a campaign. Existing drafts are preserved; unsupported entries show an explanation.

steps.title: Approve shared fields once
steps.detail: A System Manager selects allowed business fields in Template Field Policies. Insert field offers approved fields from the source DocType and readable Single DocTypes such as Hospital Settings. These choices apply to all templates using that source.

steps.title: Write and preview the message
steps.detail: Write the message next to Live Preview and use Insert field for patient name and appointment reference. In Local message mode, selecting private media changes Message Text to Caption and shows the attachment above it. Remove Media to restore text mode. Header and Footer are optional fixed text fields, each up to 60 characters on one line. The preview shows them above and below the body. Put personalized fields in Message Text; header variables are not supported.

steps.title: Prepare a Meta submission
steps.detail: In Meta mode, enter a lowercase Meta Template Name, language code and Utility or Marketing category. Provide a realistic review example for each variable. Imported numbered variables also need a Source Field mapping. Save, then an Admin chooses Meta → Submit to Meta. Saving alone makes no Meta request.

steps.title: Read the review outcome
steps.detail: Check Meta status to refresh the account catalogue. Signed review webhooks can update the status too. If Rejected, read Meta’s reason and recommendation, then the app’s suggested fix. If Meta gives no detail, open WhatsApp Manager or Business Support Home rather than guessing the cause. Edit, save and choose Submit changes to Meta when ready.

steps.title: Use the template in a campaign
steps.detail: Choose New campaign from a saved template. The campaign references this content and owns the sender, recipients, filters and sending workflow. Multiple campaigns can reuse the same template.

guides.check: The saved template contains the intended content. For Meta mode, its status applies to the exact submitted wording and sender account.
guides.note: Editors, Admins and System Managers can edit content. Only Admins and System Managers can submit to Meta or refresh Meta status. The local Meta authoring editor supports a text body, positional variables, and optional fixed text header and footer. DOCUMENT headers are managed in WhatsApp Manager. Other media headers, header variables, buttons, authentication templates and named parameters are not supported in the local Meta editor. Local messages can use private JPEG/PNG/PDF media and require an open reply window. Changing approved wording requires another Meta submission. Saving content does not activate campaigns. If a submission times out, check status before retrying. After ten minutes and a complete check finding no match, another explicit submission is permitted; nothing is resent automatically. Approved DOCUMENT-header templates created in WhatsApp Manager can be synced and used by Document delivery rules for a different private PDF per record.
guides.description: This defines the message itself: its text, optional media, reusable fields and Meta review details. Saving a draft does not submit it to Meta or send a message. Campaigns select this content and separately control recipients, sending times and automation.

guides.title: Send documents automatically
guides.summary: Send generated invoice PDFs or private report attachments when a record matches your rule.
guides.audience: Admin · System Manager, with source-record access
guides.description: WhatsApp Document Rule connects a business record, trigger, recipient, PDF and approved WhatsApp document template. Matching saved changes create a WhatsApp Document Delivery entry and use the normal outbox. Select and Data fields share a chip input; Text fields offer Equals or Contains. Comparison values belong only to the rule: they never change source records or field options.

screenshots.caption: Invoice Status uses removable chips. Typing / opens the remaining defined options.
An unsaved rule edit demonstrates a Data field with an existing value and a newly typed custom value.
An unsaved rule edit demonstrates Contains and Comparison text for a Small Text field.

steps.title: Prepare the sender and document template
steps.detail: A System Manager configures the sender and integration switches. Create a Utility template with a Document header in WhatsApp Manager, obtain approval, then open WhatsApp Phone Number ID and choose Sync approved templates. The local message editor does not author Document headers. Record recipient consent in Inbox → Details → Messaging permissions.

steps.title: Open the rule DocType
steps.detail: Open Document delivery rules in the WhatsApp sidebar, or search for WhatsApp Document Rule. Create a rule or open HMS - Invoice PDF after issue. Keep Enabled unchecked while configuring. On rule and delivery forms, Help → User guide returns here.

steps.title: Choose the source and event
steps.detail: Set Record type to the source business DocType, such as HMS Invoice. Choose Record created, Field changes to a value, or Document submitted. Submission is available only for submittable sources. For a field-change trigger, choose Trigger field from its dropdown.

steps.title: Choose values for a dropdown or Check field
steps.detail: In Send when value is, type / to open defined source options, or type /Refund to filter them. Select an option to add its chip; repeat for several. For the invoice preset, keep Issued, Partly Paid, Paid and Refund Due. A Check field offers Checked and Unchecked. Remove a chip with × or Backspace in an empty input. This input does not create new source options.

steps.title: Add custom Data values
steps.detail: Use the same chip input for a Data field. Type / to search up to 20 distinct existing values on records you can read; add text after / to narrow the results. To add a new comparison, type it without / and press Enter. For example, Ready for collection and Courier requested can be two accepted values. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Saving commits a custom value still being typed; a slash search is never stored as a comparison.

steps.title: Match Text, Small Text or Long Text
steps.detail: Choose Text matching → Equals or Contains, then fill Comparison text. Equals compares the entire text, preserving spaces and line breaks; Contains matches the exact phrase anywhere in the source text. Both are case-sensitive. Blank or whitespace-only comparisons are rejected. Changing Trigger field clears the old comparison. An Int field keeps one accepted number per line.

steps.title: Add any extra conditions
steps.detail: Every Only when row must match. For invoices, add Invoice Type equals Invoice so credit notes do not use the invoice rule. The selected trigger values form one group: entering the matching group creates a delivery; changing within that group does not resend.

steps.title: Choose the patient phone
steps.detail: Set Find phone number on to A linked record, Linked record field to Patient, and Phone field to Mobile. Use This record when the source itself holds the phone. Numbers need a country code. The execution user must retain access to the source and linked recipient.

steps.title: Choose the document source
steps.detail: For invoices, choose Generate PDF and HMS - Itemized invoice. The worker renders the triggering record and saves its PDF privately. For a completed laboratory PDF, choose Private attachment and Report file. The attachment must be a private PDF belonging to that source record.

steps.title: Map the approved message
steps.detail: Choose Sender and an Approved document template with a DOCUMENT header for that sender. Map every body variable from Record, Recipient or Fixed text. For Hello {{1}}, your invoice dated {{2}} is attached, map variable 1 to Recipient → Name and variable 2 to Record → Invoice Date.

steps.title: Save and preview
steps.detail: Save the disabled rule and choose Preview. Select a source record and check recipient, document, message and whether the trigger matches. Preview creates no PDF, outbox entry or send. Use the source record’s normal Print screen to inspect the generated layout.

steps.title: Enable the configured workflow
steps.detail: After checking approval, consent and mappings, enable the rule and save. The configuring user becomes Execution user. Enable Outbound Requests and Enable Automation in WhatsApp Settings, and run the worker and scheduler. Issue a new invoice or complete the configured source transition. Existing matching records are not backfilled automatically.

steps.title: Release, monitor or resolve a held delivery
steps.detail: Open Delivery history or WhatsApp Document Delivery. If Require staff release before sending is checked, a supervisor with source write access must choose Release document. Preparation status and Message status are separate: Queued is not Delivered. Read Action needed for Held or Failed. Retry preparation only fixes preparation; inspect the outbox for a send already created. Unknown outcomes are not automatically resent. Prepare current document explicitly handles an eligible current source/rule version.

guides.check: The rule uses the right source field and comparison, recipient phone, private PDF and approved document template. Source records and source-field definitions stay unchanged. Check the actual WhatsApp delivery status rather than treating a queued or accepted request as delivered.
guides.note: Only Whatsapp Admin and System Manager can configure these rules, and source/recipient permissions still apply. Data suggestions respect record query permissions; selected dropdown values come from the source field. Local presets remain disabled until configured with approved DOCUMENT-header templates. Meta approval and actual recipient delivery require separate verification.

guides.title: Send a reviewed laboratory report
guides.summary: Send the patient’s completed private PDF after clinical review and explicit staff release.
guides.audience: Clinical staff for review · Admin or System Manager for messaging release
guides.description: The HMS - Released laboratory report preset watches Lab Report → Status = Reviewed, resolves the linked patient’s Mobile number, and uses the private PDF in Report file. It requires an additional messaging release. A reviewed status alone does not send the report.

screenshots.caption: The laboratory preset matches Reviewed and requires staff release before sending.
The linked Patient supplies Mobile, while Private attachment uses Report file.

steps.title: Prepare the hospital sender and consent
steps.detail: Configure the sender, obtain approval for a report-notification template with a Document header, and Sync approved templates on the sender. Check the patient’s country-code phone number and recorded messaging consent. Keep the preset disabled during setup.

steps.title: Open the laboratory preset
steps.detail: Open WhatsApp Document Rule → HMS - Released laboratory report. Set Record type to Lab Report, Trigger to Field changes to a value, and Trigger field to Status.

steps.title: Select Reviewed and keep the release step
steps.detail: In Send when value is, type /Reviewed and choose Reviewed as a chip. Keep Require staff release before sending checked. For the existing preset these values are already selected. Only when conditions can further narrow the rule; every added row must match.

steps.title: Map the linked patient and actual PDF
steps.detail: Choose A linked record → Patient → Mobile. Set Document source to Private attachment and Attachment field to Report file. Select the configured Sender and Approved document template, then map each body variable. Use the actual completed result PDF attached to this Lab Report.

steps.title: Save, preview and enable the rule
steps.detail: Save and Preview a readable source report. The preview checks configuration without creating a PDF or sending. Complete template approval and mappings, then enable the rule and required WhatsApp integration switches. A worker must be available.

steps.title: Complete the source report and clinical review
steps.detail: In Lab Report, attach the completed private PDF to Report file and fill Received On. HMS requires both the received date and private file for Received or Reviewed reports. Clinical staff review the results and save Status = Reviewed. Configure the rule before this transition; previously reviewed reports are not automatically backfilled.

steps.title: Release the matching delivery
steps.detail: Open the rule’s Delivery history, then the matching WhatsApp Document Delivery in Awaiting release. A Whatsapp Admin or System Manager with write access to the source report checks the patient, current report and PDF, then chooses Release document. The worker prepares the attachment and queues the approved message.

steps.title: Check the patient delivery outcome
steps.detail: Check Message status or View message delivery for accepted, delivered, read, failed, held or unknown outcomes. Preparation status alone is not proof of patient delivery. If held, correct the stated issue before using the appropriate retry action.

steps.title: Handle existing or changed reports deliberately
steps.detail: An enabled rule’s Prepare current document action can create a delivery for an eligible existing source version, subject to the same release requirement. HMS protects reviewed report status, file and review details. Do not alter them to force a send. Changed source/rule versions and uncertain provider outcomes require review; do not repeatedly create new messages.

guides.check: The source Lab Report is clinically reviewed, its completed PDF is private and belongs to that report, the linked patient’s phone is correct, and staff release is recorded before sending. Verify the actual delivery outcome in the message log.
guides.note: Clinical authorization to review a result and WhatsApp authority to release a document are separate permissions. The preset’s Test number sender label is local configuration; choose the hospital’s configured sender and approved document template before enabling. A blank laboratory worksheet is not a completed result report.

guides.title: Activate a campaign for document events
guides.summary: Queue a patient update when an appointment-related record changes.

screenshots.caption: An event campaign references shared content and selects the Update event.
Automation Active and Run As belong to the campaign.

steps.title: Choose the event
steps.detail: Open the Appointment status update campaign and select the event matching your hospital process. The walkthrough uses Update on an appointment follow-up task. Use Update Field and Target Field for a specific field change.

steps.title: Review recipients and content
steps.detail: Check the selected Message Template, sender, recipient field and source filters. Edit wording and approved fields from the template; change the audience here.

steps.title: Activate and save
steps.detail: Clear Disable, enable Automation Active and save. Run As records the activating user. A System Manager must separately enable the required integration switches.

steps.title: Inspect event runs
steps.detail: Perform the intended business action only when ready. Open Campaign Runs and filter Document events to inspect the resulting record and send outcomes.

guides.check: The matching business action creates a durable event run in the same transaction. A rolled-back source change cannot dispatch its message.
guides.note: The activating user must keep the app role and source permissions. Disable the campaign or clear Automation Active to stop new event runs; already in-flight provider requests may finish. A date becoming due is not a record-update event. Use a Date Reminder campaign for follow-up and OP-validity reminders.
guides.description: This automatically starts a message run when a business record undergoes a selected change, such as creation, update or submission. The app applies the saved campaign to that record and prepares messages for its recipients. The campaign must be active, and the user it runs as must still have the required access.

guides.title: Create or pause a schedule
guides.summary: Run daily appointment reminders or schedule a one-time follow-up.

screenshots.caption: Create or update schedule: campaign, local occurrence, recurrence and timezone.

steps.title: Open New schedule
steps.detail: Open Templates & Automation → Campaign Runs and choose New schedule, or choose Create schedule on a saved campaign.

steps.title: Choose the campaign and time
steps.detail: Select the Appointment confirmation campaign. For a one-time follow-up enter First occurrence (local time) and leave Recurrence blank. For daily 09:00 reminders use 0 9 * * * in Recurrence.

steps.title: Confirm the timezone
steps.detail: Use an explicit timezone such as Asia/Kolkata. Save schedule. Check the resulting Schedule record’s state, Run As and Next Due At.

steps.title: Pause or resume
steps.detail: Open the Schedule record and use Pause or Resume. Editors control their own schedules; Admin and System Manager can supervise others. Review each resulting run in Campaign Runs. To stop a recurring campaign, pause it and review existing queued work.

guides.check: The durable Schedule record controls future occurrences. Saving a schedule does not override disabled outbound or automation switches.
guides.note: Missed occurrences within one hour may catch up once; older occurrences are skipped. Ambiguous or invalid daylight-saving local times are rejected. Pausing cannot recall a provider request already in flight.
guides.description: This runs a saved campaign at a chosen future time or on a repeating schedule. The app uses the selected timezone to work out when each run is due, then prepares messages for the records selected by the campaign. You can pause a schedule to stop it from starting further work and resume it when needed.

guides.title: Configure and run a campaign
guides.summary: Choose reusable content, recipients and the sending workflow.
guides.audience: Editor · Admin · System Manager; bulk start requires Admin or System Manager

screenshots.caption: Campaigns reference a template and separately configure sender, recipients, scope and workflow.
A bulk preview lists personalized messages before the explicit Start campaign action.

steps.title: Choose a reusable template
steps.detail: Open Templates & Automation → Campaigns or choose New campaign on Appointment confirmation. Give the campaign a recognizable name such as Tomorrow’s appointment reminders. Select Message Template and Sender. The source DocType is taken from the template; Open template lets you edit its content separately.

steps.title: Select recipients and scope
steps.detail: Choose the patient phone field or reusable recipients. Use Set Query to select the appointment follow-ups to process. The fictional walkthrough uses OPD-1042 and OPD-1043. Keep Disabled checked while preparing the campaign.

steps.title: Choose the sending workflow
steps.detail: Use Custom or None for an action on a business record; a document Event for automatic changes; or Scheduled/Cron for future runs. Enable Automation Active for events and schedules. For a bulk run, select Send to filtered records (bulk), save and clear Disabled when ready.

steps.title: Remind patients before a date
steps.detail: Choose Event = Date Reminder and a Reminder Date Field. For Patient follow-ups choose Follow Up; for OP expiry choose Validity Expiring On. Set Start Reminders (Days Before) to 2, Daily Reminder Time to 09:00 and the timezone to Asia/Kolkata. This sends at 9 AM two days before, one day before and on the due date. Use additional filters to exclude disabled patients. Automation Active creates the daily schedule when the campaign is saved and enabled.

steps.title: Preview a bulk run
steps.detail: An Admin opens Campaign Runs → Preview campaign and selects the saved campaign. Review every page of personalized messages, recipients and exclusions. Previewing does not send. Repeated family phone numbers receive a separate message per source record.

steps.title: Start and monitor
steps.detail: Choose Start campaign after review. Check record processing separately from delivery status. Pause, Resume or Cancel remaining work from the run controls when needed.

guides.check: The run creates one message per business record and recipient, deduplicating repeated recipients only within that record.
guides.note: Campaigns start Disabled. Enable only after reviewing the audience and content. Meta campaigns must use a sender from the same WABA as the template. Both campaign and shared template edits invalidate older previews and queued versions. Existing queued work may be held for review after the split; it is never automatically resent. Completed means record processing finished, not that every message was delivered. Global switches, consent, source permissions and sender eligibility still apply. Date reminders need the scheduler running. They recheck the date before sending and hold stale messages if the date changes. Use a Meta-approved template when recipients may be outside the reply window.
guides.description: This controls who receives a reusable message and when it should be prepared. A campaign selects a template, sender, recipient fields and record filters. It can support a manual action, a document event, a schedule or a reviewed bulk run. The message content and Meta approval stay on the selected template.

guides.title: Check delivery and handle blocked sends
guides.summary: Check whether patient messages were queued, blocked or delivered.

screenshots.caption: Automation run results show each request’s state and a link to its conversation.

steps.title: Find the request
steps.detail: Use the conversation timeline or Campaign Runs → View details. Admin and System Manager can also open Administration → Outbound Queue and Send Attempts.

steps.title: Read the status
steps.detail: In the Inbox, Waiting to send means the message is queued. Accepted by WhatsApp means WhatsApp has accepted it, but delivery has not been confirmed yet. Sent, Delivered and Read show later updates. Needs attention means sending is on hold; ask an administrator to check the reason.

steps.title: Handle confirmed failures
steps.detail: Review the reason and fix the issue first. Retry confirmed failure is available only for a known unaccepted failure. Cancel send applies only to eligible requests before a network attempt starts.

steps.title: Check an unconfirmed send before sending again
steps.detail: Send status not confirmed means the app does not know whether WhatsApp sent the message. Check its history and delivery updates before composing another message to avoid sending twice. The same uncertain request is not retried automatically. In administration screens, this status is called Unknown.

guides.check: You know whether work is queued, blocked, accepted or actually delivered. Run totals separate record expansion from send outcomes.
guides.note: Editors can inspect their permitted run details; campaigns and administration diagnostics require Admin or System Manager. For delayed work, ask your System Manager to check switches, sender state, scheduler and workers.
guides.description: This shows what happened to messages after they were queued, helping you find delays and failures. You can check whether a request is waiting, blocked, accepted by the provider or delivered, and review any available reason for a problem. The available controls let you cancel eligible unsent requests or retry confirmed unaccepted failures.

guides.title: Configure a sender and integration
guides.summary: Configure the hospital’s Patient Services sender and integration switches.

screenshots.caption: Riverbend Patient Services sender account with masked training credentials.
WhatsApp Settings: independent outbound, inbound and automation switches; secrets remain masked.
Import dialog: select reusable content from the Meta catalogue; existing and unsupported entries remain visible.

steps.title: Open sender accounts
steps.detail: Open Administration → Phone Numbers and add a WhatsApp Phone Number ID. Quick Entry shows Label, Phone Number ID, Access Token and Enabled. Set Label to Riverbend Patient Services and enter the hospital’s correct external Phone Number ID. Leave Enabled off while preparing the account.

steps.title: Enter account credentials
steps.detail: A System Manager enters Access Token. Choose Edit Full Form to add WABA ID and optional account details. Portfolio Id is the optional Meta business portfolio identifier used to group contacts across sender accounts; when blank, contact grouping falls back to WABA ID or the individual sender. Credentials remain restricted to System Manager.

steps.title: Review integration settings
steps.detail: Open WhatsApp Settings. Review API configuration and, for inbound delivery, the application secret and verification token. Enable Outbound Requests, Enable Inbound and Enable Automation are separate switches and default off.

steps.title: Enable only when ready
steps.detail: Confirm the account and integration configuration before enabling the required switches and sender. A worker and scheduler must be running for queued and scheduled work. An Admin can then use Sync approved templates on the sender form.

steps.title: Select templates to import
steps.detail: On the saved Riverbend Patient Services sender, choose Sync approved templates. The dialog lists all Meta templates with language, review status and a message preview. Choose a Source DocType, select the supported entries you need and choose Import selected. Already-imported records are linked and preserved. Unsupported formats show why they cannot be imported.

guides.check: Sync refreshes the Meta catalogue for the WABA. Import selected adds only your chosen supported templates to the local library, without creating campaigns or sending messages.
guides.note: Screenshots show fictional test configuration. They are not working credentials. Enabling outbound permits real provider requests on a configured live site; this guide does not enable anything for you.
guides.description: This connects a WhatsApp business phone number to the app and gives it a recognizable account name. A System Manager enters its account details and credentials and controls whether sending, receiving and automation are enabled. Message rules and conversations then use that configured account as their sender.

guides.title: Review inbound and webhook issues
guides.summary: Investigate incoming patient messages and delivery receipts.

screenshots.caption: Quarantined webhook event with its safe reason and Replay event action.

steps.title: Check inbound configuration
steps.detail: Ask your System Manager to confirm inbound capture, sender mapping, application secret and verification token. The callback is /api/method/whatsapp_messaging.messaging.webhooks.receive on the site’s reachable HTTPS domain.

steps.title: Open Webhook events
steps.detail: In Administration open Webhook events and filter Failed or Quarantined. Check the sender mapping, event state and safe error reason. Raw payloads are restricted to System Manager.

steps.title: Resolve the cause
steps.detail: Correct a missing account mapping or configuration issue before replaying. Do not repeatedly replay an unresolved event.

steps.title: Replay and verify
steps.detail: For a Failed or Quarantined event, choose Replay event. Check its new state, then inspect the affected conversation or message receipt.

guides.check: Valid events create or update the appropriate message history. Duplicate provider events are handled once; late status receipts do not regress delivery.
guides.note: Public HTTPS routing and Meta callback configuration must be set up separately by the System Manager. An event list alone does not prove a live callback is configured.
guides.description: This handles incoming updates from WhatsApp, including received messages and delivery receipts. If an update cannot be processed, an Admin can inspect its state and error reason, correct the cause and request another processing attempt. These updates keep conversation history and delivery status current.

guides.title: Manage reusable recipients
guides.summary: Keep the reception coordinator’s contact available for local rules.
guides.audience: Admin · System Manager (Editors can select existing recipients)

screenshots.caption: Reception coordinator contact with the country code and phone number entered.

steps.title: Open Recipients
steps.detail: From Messaging choose Recipients and add a Static Recipient named Reception coordinator.

steps.title: Enter a recognizable label and phone
steps.detail: Enter Label. In Phone Number, select the country code and enter the national number. Save the recipient.

steps.title: Select it on a template
steps.detail: Open the intended local template and select the entry in Other Recipients when the workflow requires an additional recipient.

steps.title: Review before sending
steps.detail: Confirm the source recipient field and additional recipients together. A repeated number is deduplicated within each business record.

guides.check: The recipient can be reused on local rules. Saving a recipient does not create a conversation, record consent or send a message.
guides.note: For a campaign, the same recipient can receive different messages for different source records. Consent and suppression rules still apply.
guides.description: This saves a named phone contact that can be reused in message rules. An Admin enters the name and number once, and users can select that contact under Other Recipients when configuring a rule. Saving a contact alone does not send a message or record consent.

guides.title: Read messages and preserved history
guides.summary: Refer to patient conversations, individual messages and preserved history.

screenshots.caption: Canonical message record showing its status, content and account.

steps.title: Use the inbox first
steps.detail: The inbox combines canonical incoming and outgoing messages for a specific sender and recipient. Open the thread to view its timeline.

steps.title: Look up individual records
steps.detail: Messaging → Messages opens message records; Conversations opens conversation records. Use list filters to locate the relevant entry.

steps.title: Recognize preserved legacy data
steps.detail: Older records remain available as history. They are not automatically assigned a guessed account or relabeled as delivered.

steps.title: Use workflow actions for changes
steps.detail: Queue new messages from the inbox or configured record actions. Use assignment and status controls in the inbox instead of editing history records.

guides.check: You can refer to the stored history without changing the evidence of past sends. Canonical operational records are read-only through ordinary forms.
guides.note: Historical messages are never automatically resent. If an old record has no reliable account or inbound window, use a correctly configured current conversation for new work.
guides.description: This lets users review stored messages and conversations to understand what was sent or received and check recorded statuses. The inbox provides the conversation timeline, while message records provide individual details. Preserved older records remain available for reference without automatically sending them again.
